sentences.text:
Shri Anubhav Jain - Public Prosecutor for respondent/Sta
Shri R. K. Vishwakarma - Advocate for complainant.
Heard on I.A. No.5912 of 2023.

This is the first application seeking for suspension of sentence and bail filed on behalf of appellant Sunil who has been convicted under Sections 450, 376(2)(a) and 376(2)(N) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years, 15 years (on two counts) and fine of Rs.5,000/- and Rs.10,000/- (on two counts) respectively with default stipulations.
This application has been filed on the ground that the matter has been compromised between the parties.
The victim was a major.
Appellant and victim were known to each other.
She has made relations with her own will with the appellant.
The appellant has already divorced the first wife in terms of the traditions which are followed in their community.
Affidavit to the aforesaid effect has been filed by the first wife which is placed on record by way of an application - I.A. No.10897 of 2023.
The appellant as well as the victim were residing together for several years.
The appellant is in custody since 02.03.2023.
Therefore, he prays for grant of bail.

State counsel has vehemently opposed the application stating that the appellant was already a married person and without legally divorcing the first wife he has made physical relations with the victim and now presently residing with the victim.
Merely the fact that the victim is a major and the appellant wants to marry her cannot be a ground to enlarge the appellant on bail as the guilt is proved before the learned trial court.
He has prayed for dismissal of the application.
Considering the facts and circumstances, the material available on record and without commenting on the merits of the case, this court deems it fit to enlarge the appellant on bail.
I.A. No.5912 of 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is allowed.
